reviewScope.summary: PR #55, EDU-03. Review of two learner-facing examples and one focused test, commit 003924586c73c0971d4a470a7ebf52865fd92804, against master 35214e45b0b0ffdf2444e48934f3612b1468b087. Technical, pedagogical, accessibility and adversarial model review; not independent human review.
evidence: Inspected all three GitHub PR #55 file patches. Source changes are confined to two existing Learn-card idea strings; session/card IDs, select answers, feedback, XP, storage and navigation are unchanged.

Python introductory text adds print(type(45)) with the real Python representation <class 'int'>, ahead of a subsequent print(type("7")) check; preserves learner ability to distinguish int versus str. Original numeric/text example remains.
UX/UU text adds a concrete departure-time example for an image-only timetable. It illustrates the need for machine-readable text and does not claim that one assistive format works for everyone.
Focused regression test pins the unchanged response IDs str and tekst and the corresponding alternatives; no application mechanism or code execution was changed.

Owner-provided isolated Windows transcript: 80 targeted tests in 3 files passed; formatting, lint, TypeScript, Vite build and bundle budget passed; JS gzip 465409/470000 with zero bundle violations or warnings. Reviewer did not independently rerun tests.
No source overlap with A2 Kanban/SQL changes or A1 Settings/E2E changes. UX/UU starts after the original first 24 Utviklerblikk sessions that are protected by a separate fingerprint.
Hosted GitHub Actions run 41043094196 failed before full release validation due only to missing review binding for payload tree 904594e6922ab63e7b80ebb194a40e2604016160.
Owner approved combined model review and requests no supplementary owner or Codex review unless specific material risk exists.

adversarialFindings.description: Introducing type() could mistakenly imply that 45 and "45" are interchangeable or show an inaccurate interpreter representation.
adversarialFindings.resolution: The example uses exact Python output and retains distinction between numeric int and quoted string, while preserving original exercise and answer.

adversarialFindings.description: The raw output includes Python terminology class that is not separately defined at this point.
adversarialFindings.resolution: The precise output is shown and context explains it as the value type; a fuller class explanation is deliberately out of scope. The next exercise tests int versus str, not object-oriented terminology.

adversarialFindings.description: Image-only timetable example could imply a blanket accessibility rule that all image content must be duplicated in full.
adversarialFindings.resolution: It specifically asks for the essential departure information to be readable as text and retains the original warning about differing needs and insufficient one-off tests.

adversarialFindings.description: Pedagogical copy edits could silently alter progress or correct answers.
adversarialFindings.resolution: No structural IDs or learner-state contracts changed; regression checks existing correctId and answer order for both practices.

adversarialFindings.description: Review is model-authored in the same conversation, not independent human verification.
adversarialFindings.resolution: Reviewer identity is explicit and owner authorizes proportionate combined model review; mandatory hosted gate remains.

retrospective.summary: Bounded review supports proceeding to authoritative hosted release certification, not immediate merge or production promotion. No independent human review, browser certification, or production readiness is claimed. Avoid extra owner review loops unless CI reveals a substantive defect.
